subject.title: feat(ui): complete Control UI MCP App bridge

question: Should every app/widget-originated prompt remain restricted to conversational text by rejecting host-only bang commands as well as slash commands before the normal chat dispatcher?
rationale: This is an intentional authority boundary between sandboxed third-party UI and host command handling; code can mechanically enforce the safer rule, but the permanent product/security contract needs owner confirmation.

options.title: Reject bang commands before dispatch
options.body: Extend the shared validator to reject `!` alongside `/`, retain a single send seam, and add regression tests for both MCP Apps and widget prompts.

options.title: Allow host-command syntax deliberately
options.body: Keep the current predicate only if maintainers explicitly define consent and authorization semantics for app-triggered host commands.

recommendation.title: Reject bang commands before dispatch
recommendation.body: Extend the shared validator to reject `!` alongside `/`, retain a single send seam, and add regression tests for both MCP Apps and widget prompts.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current bridge implementation and are already assigned to the PR; a deeper current-main history owner could not be verified in the read-only runner.
